chunks: The scholar and jurist Abu Ja'far Muhammad ibn Ali ibn al-Husayn ibn Musa ibn Babawayh al-Qummi (may God have mercy on him) narrated to us. He said: My father (may God be pleased with him) narrated to us. He said: Sa'd ibn Abdullah narrated to us. He said: Ahmad ibn Abi Abdullah narrated to us. He said: My father narrated to us from Muhammad ibn Abi Umayr, from Malik ibn Anas, from al-Sadiq Ja'far ibn Muhammad, from his father, from his forefathers (peace be upon them), from Ali (peace be upon him) who said:

The poor came to the Messenger of God (may God bless him and his family) and said: O Messenger of God, the rich have the means to free slaves, and we do not. They have the means to perform the pilgrimage, and we do not. They have the means to give in charity, and we do not. They have the means to wage jihad, and we do not.

So he (may God bless him and his family) said: Whoever exalts God, Blessed and Exalted, one hundred times, it is better than freeing one hundred slaves. Whoever glorifies God one hundred times, it is better than sacrificing one hundred camels. Whoever praises God one hundred times, it is better than supplying one hundred horses in the way of God with their saddles, bridles, and riders. And whoever says "there is no god but God" one hundred times, he will be the best of people in deeds that day, except he who exceeds him.

He said: The rich were told about that and they began practicing it. He said: So the poor returned to the Prophet (may God bless him and his family) and said: O Messenger of God, the rich have been told what you said and they began practicing it. So he (may God bless him and his family) said: That is the bounty of God; He gives it to whomever He wills.

key_terms.تكبير: Takbir - saying "Allahu Akbar" (God is the Greatest)
key_terms.تهليل: Tahlil - saying "La ilaha illallah" (There is no god but God)

ai.seo_question: What did the Prophet say about dhikr being better than charity and freeing slaves?
ai.summary: In this hadith narrated through the family of the Prophet (SAWW) via Imam Ali (AS), the poor companions complained to the Prophet that the rich could earn merit through freeing slaves, performing hajj, giving charity, and participating in jihad -- all requiring wealth. The Prophet responded that dhikr (remembrance of God) through takbir, tasbih, tahmid, and tahlil -- each recited one hundred times -- surpasses all these acts. When the rich also adopted this practice, the Prophet concluded with the Quranic verse "That is the bounty of God; He gives it to whomever He wills" (62:4), teaching that divine grace is not restricted by material circumstances.

en.bilal-muhammad: Muhammad b. Ali b. al-Husayn b. Musa b. Babuwayh al-Qummi (rh) narrated to us. He said: My father (ra) narrated to us. He said: Sa`d b. `Abdullah narrated to us. He said: Ahmad b. Abi `Abdullah narrated to us. He said: My father narrated to us from Muhammad b. Abi Umayr from Malik b. Anas from al-Sadiq Ja`far b. Muhammad from his father from his forefathers (as) from `Ali (as).

He said: The poor came to the Messenger of Allah (s) and said: O Messenger of Allah! The rich have those who they could emancipate, and we do not. They have that which they could use for pilgrimages, and we do not. They have that which they could give in charity, and we do not. They have that which they could use for jihad, and we do not.

So, the Messenger of Allah (s) said: "Exalting Allah (takbir) one hundred times is better than freeing one hundred slaves. Glorifying Allah (subhanallah) one hundred times is better than sacrificing one hundred camels. Praising Allah (alhamdulillah) one hundred times is better than supplying one hundred readied horses with a horseman going in the cause of Allah. Whomever says: "there is no god except Allah" (la ilaha illallah) one hundred times, he will be the better than the people in deeds that day, except he who exceeds him.

So, the rich were told about that, and they began practicing it. So, the poor returned to the Prophet (s) and said: O Messenger of Allah! The rich were told about what you had said, and they began practicing it. So, he (s) said: That is the virtue of Allah, which He gives to whomever He pleases.
